title: Cosmic Fractions: Navigating Unlike Denominators with Space Stations
subject: Mathematics
target_skill: Adding fractions with unlike denominators using visual fraction bars

aligned_standards.description: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators by finding common denominators.
aligned_standards.subject: Mathematics

sections.title: Step 1: The Space Docking Problem (Why Units Must Match)
sections.content: Imagine Rocket A carries 1/2 tank of fuel and Rocket B carries 1/4 tank. We cannot simply add the tank parts together directly because the containers are cut into different sized pieces! To combine them, we need both containers partitioned into the same size compartments (fourths).
sections.check_for_understanding_question: Why can't we add 1/2 and 1/4 by just adding 1+1 on top and 2+4 on bottom?
sections.check_answer: Because 1/2 and 1/4 represent different sized slices/pieces.

sections.title: Step 2: Scaling Fractions with Visual Fraction Bars
sections.content: Look at the visual fraction bar: 1/2 is the exact same length as 2/4. When we replace 1/2 with 2/4, our math problem becomes 2/4 + 1/4. Now that both parts have the common denominator 4, we simply add the numerators: 2 fourths + 1 fourth = 3 fourths (3/4).
sections.check_for_understanding_question: What equivalent fraction with denominator 4 has the same value as 1/2?

practice_exercises.prompt: Using a fraction bar model, find 1/3 + 1/6.
practice_exercises.hint_tier_1_concept: Can 1/3 be sliced into equal sixths?
practice_exercises.hint_tier_2_strategy: Multiply both numerator and denominator of 1/3 by 2 to find equivalent sixths.
practice_exercises.visual_aid_description: Fraction bar showing 1/3 divided into two 1/6 segments.

practice_exercises.hint_tier_1_concept: What is the common denominator between 5 and 10?
